title: project-intent
body: overview/project-intent — viola is a hybrid local developer tool that lets one interactive Claude Code session drive another on the user's own subscription. It has a native Linux CLI binary and a Claude Code plugin of hooks and a stdio MCP server that calls that binary; a keyboard-driven terminal fleet console is planned, not built. It wraps the unmodified claude CLI in a PTY, types at turn boundaries, answers dialogs through hooks, and holds a one-driver wheel the human can take at any moment. It is a modular monolith: one binary with internal crates around core, and no daemon.

It wraps the unmodified claude CLI in a PTY, types at turn boundaries, answers dialogs through hooks, and holds a one-driver wheel the human can take at any moment. It is a modular monolith: one binary with internal crates around core, and no daemon.

data.why: A pre-existing foreign, permissive or symlinked diagnostics file is never written.

body: - Performance budget regression (hyperfine `max` gate)

- **Boundary:** Session id as a child argv value (`viola revive`, `viola verify`'s Run E)
  - **What to validate:** The id handed to the child after `--resume` is the newest logged `agent_session_id` of the session-id shape, or the `--id` value when the instance's log holds it. An `--id` the log does not hold, or a log with no session, is `no-session`: exit 1 before any spawn. The shape is closed (`viola_agent_claude::is_session_id`: 36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18 and 23, ASCII hex elsewhere), and a malformed `--id` is a clap usage error (exit 2). The id is one argv element of a direct spawn, never a shell, built only by `viola_agent_claude::resume_args` (`--resume <id>`, then `--fork-session` when `--fork` is given), after the wrapper's `--plugin-dir <dir>` and before the words after `--`. A third source, inside `viola verify`: Run E takes the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture through `viola_agent_claude::ledger::resume_target`, only when `is_session_id` accepts it (with none Run E spawns nothing and `resume-session` fails), and hands it to `resume_args(id, false)` (no `--fork-session`), after Run E's run args and its `--plugin-dir` pair, with no `--settings`. `revive --list` prints only ids of that shape. No refusal line or hint holds the recorded directory, a pid or a logged id. **Ratified:** a value read from the log and placed on a child's command line is a crossing the founder ratified (live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer), shown to him as a crossing with two options: ratify it, or allow only an id the human types. The third source is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows («Run E, шестой старт», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`).
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-agent-claude` `is_session_id` / `resume_args` (the one product home of the two flag literals); `src/cmd/revive.rs`; `viola_state::replay::session_chain`; `ledger::resume_target` and `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` `resume_run` (Run E)
- Unhandled panics (always): the one-line `event:"panic"`.
| callsign | `\x1b[1m` (bold) | `\x1b[1m` | `\x1b[1m` | NAME column values |

- **Entity:** on-disk event log `instances/<name>/events.ndjson` (prompts and assistant output, high classification) plus the design cross-lane CL-1 `send-issued` / `send-refused` events
  - **Source:** arch excerpt, On-disk (Event line); security excerpt, Data Classifications (Prompts, Tool args); creator excerpt, Founder Direction 5
  - **Testability:** testable (temp `--home` + fake agent, per the security excerpt's testability hint)

- **[Deployment / Distribution] `cargo install --path .`, with the plugin compiled into the binary (KEYSTONE).** `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` are embedded via `include_str!`, and `plugin.json`'s version comes from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. At start, `viola run` copies its own exe to `<viola home>/bin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/viola` if that copy is absent, and re-hashes an existing copy before reusing it: a copy that no longer matches refuses the start (exit 1, `pinned-hash-mismatch`) and is left as found.
 It rewrites the plugin files on every start to `<viola home>/plugin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/` and substitutes the copy's path (forward slashes) into every exec-form `command` in `hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`. It then passes that folder with `--plugin-dir`, sets `VIOLA_BIN` to the copy and puts the copy's folder first on the child's PATH. `hooks.json` registers seven exec-form entries, each `"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@"` (substituted at start) with `"args": ["hook", "<kebab event>"]`: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop with `"timeout": 5`; SessionEnd with no `timeout` key; Notification, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure with `"async": true`. The dialog tier joins them (chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id): PreToolUse with `"matcher": "AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode"` and PermissionRequest, each with `"timeout": 3615` — nine exec-form entries in all. `.mcp.json` registers the server `viola` as `{"mcpServers": {"viola": {"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@", "args": ["mcp"]}}}`, the pinned copy's absolute path substituted at every start (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers; until the `mcp` verb existed it shipped `{"mcpServers": {}}`, on the operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan that a registered command that exits 2 would block Claude Code). A registered `viola mcp` that exits 1 (its home refused by `home_passes`) does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs that server's connection as failed (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings/evidence/live-round.md`). Hooks and MCP never search PATH. Rationale: the binary and the plugin can no longer drift apart. The prototype proved that PATH-found hooks run a different binary from the wrapper after a rebuild.
 The content hash is part of the key because `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` stays `0.1.0` across development rebuilds, so the version alone would collide. A rebuild therefore never changes what a running session calls. Known trade-off: a hook fix applies only to sessions started after the rebuild. The per-frame `v` + sender version stays as the second safety net, for the optional user-level install (`viola plugin install`), which is not bound to a wrapper's pinned copy.

- NEVER use Linux abstract-namespace sockets (no filesystem permissions).

- **IPC boundaries** (viola-channel JSON-RPC over interprocess 2.4.4 local sockets):
  - `corr` carries the JSON-RPC `id` on channel lines, `dialog_id` on dialog and hook lines, and the send `cursor` on send lines (tests).
  - **Additive `conn` field (D-10).** The client generates `conn = "<process>-<pid>-<t0>-<n>"`, with `t0` the process's start instant in Unix epoch milliseconds (captured once at init; Low sensitivity like `pid`) and `n` a per-process connection counter (D-32), and sends it in `params` alongside `v` / `sender` / `from`. Both sides log it on `channel-request` / `channel-response`. It is wire-safe under arch Mixed-version tolerance, because readers skip unknown fields. A server receiving a frame without `conn` from an older peer logs `srv_conn = "srv-<accept counter>"` instead, and so does a server receiving a `conn` outside the shape `^[a-z]+-\d+-\d+-\d+$` or over 64 bytes (a peer-supplied value is logged only in that shape). The server strips `conn` from `params` before dispatch: it is never an input to a method.
  - **Join key.** The merged-log join key for channel lines is `(conn, corr)`, and `instance` is deliberately **not** part of it (D-25).
    - `conn` is unique across the session home (`<process>-<pid>-<t0>-<n>`, D-10, D-32). `<pid>` alone is not unique: PIDs are recycled. Every `hook` process opens exactly one connection (`n` = 1) and sends the same first JSON-RPC `id`, so without `t0` two hook calls from a reused PID would share `(conn, corr)`.
    - Each side logs its **own** instance. `cli` and `mcp` log the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`, which is also `from`. `run` logs the wrapper's `ViolaName`. So the two sides of one call carry different `instance` values.
    - `srv_conn` lines from older peers have no client-side counterpart. They join only within the server's own file.
  - **`cli` instance precedence** (init step 3): the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` comes first. The explicit target `ViolaName` argument becomes `instance`, and names the `cli-<name>.ndjson` file, only when `VIOLA_NAME` is unset. So `viola send --to B` run by driver A logs `instance:"A"` to `cli-A.ndjson`.
  - `agent-run logs --instance B` therefore shows only B's side of a call. To reach the caller, take `conn` from B's `channel-request` and query with no `--instance` filter, for example `agent-run logs | jq -c 'select(.record.conn=="cli-4812-1790219525118-1")'`.
  - **Send cursor on early refusals.** The arch `send` result returns `cursor` only on success or `unconfirmable`; a refusal result carries `refusal` + `detail` only. For a send refused before `send-issued` (`human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `input-not-ready`, `turn-running`), the wrapper's `send-refused` carries `corr` = the target's `events.ndjson` end offset at the moment of refusal. This value is a log join key only. It is never returned to the caller and is not a `wait after` value. After `send-issued`, every `send-*` line carries the issued cursor. The cursor alone is not a unique send key. Refusals at an unchanged end offset can share it, and a later issued send can reuse it.
  - **Send ↔ channel link (D-30).** Every wrapper `send-*` line also carries `conn` (or `srv_conn` for an older peer) and `rpc_id`, the JSON-RPC `id` of the `send` request it answers. The pair `(conn, rpc_id)` on a send line equals `(conn, corr)` on that call's `channel-request` / `channel-response`, on both sides. So the caller reaches the wrapper's send lines, and the wrapper's send lines reach the caller, without timestamp guessing. One send is identified by target `instance` + `corr` + `conn` + `rpc_id`.
  - `from` is logged with the constant companion `from_trust:"self-reported"` and is never treated as identity.
  - JSON-RPC notifications (`hook.event`) have no `id`, so their `channel-request` has a null `corr`. They join through `hook_event` + `instance` + `timestamp`.

- **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused `budget-paused`; human keys are never blocked and a running turn finishes; the pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`; the gate never polls and fails open. Rationale: the per-model weekly window is hidden, so thresholds are set low; the user's global statusline config is never touched.

- **[Links] A link `driver → driven` is recorded when a `send` or `answer` is issued from inside a wrapped session to another instance, or by an explicit `viola link <driver> <driven>`. `viola unlink` removes it.** Links are events in the log, the snapshot's link set derived by replaying them; the implicit link and the explicit verbs are built, the verbs checking the driven instance's files before any log and its wrapper serving `link` / `unlink`. **Security tier:** `Minimal (0), with targeted elevations for the local privilege boundary`
_Justification: viola is a local-only, single-user tool. It has no accounts, no public network listener, no database, no stored credentials and no regulated data (Sections 1, 3, 4, 5), which rules out Standard's user-account and HTTPS concerns and Hardened's compliance drivers. It still goes beyond a plain Minimal profile in two ways. First, the local IPC endpoint is effectively a code-execution interface (`send` types prompts, `answer` can allow PermissionRequest tool calls). It currently has no decided enforcement of its same-OS-user boundary, and its socket name is predictable, the socket standing in a per-user 0700 directory. Second, several state files decide what code runs and whether dialogs are answered: `snapshot.json`'s `statusline_command`, the `hooks.json` exec paths, the pinned binaries and the ledger stamps. The baseline is therefore Minimal (dependency audit, input validation on config and external payloads, error sanitization). On top of it sit specific local-boundary items: IPC endpoint access control and server impersonation, bracketed-paste breakout in `send.text`, and integrity of `~/.viola/`. Each of these traces to Section 2._

    - `send-*` lines with a cursor `corr` are emitted only by the target wrapper (`side:"wrapper"`, D-27), so the jq `instance` predicate is the target's. The caller-side `send-refused{side:"client"}` has `corr` null and is read from the caller's `channel-response{conn}` and `process-exit` instead.
    - The harness `--instance` filter is still not used. It would also drop the caller's `channel-*` lines, which carry the caller's instance (see Trace context propagation).
    - The `event` filter keeps out an unrelated `channel-request` whose JSON-RPC `id` happens to be 412.
    - The `channel-*` lines of the same send are reached from a matched send line: its `(conn, rpc_id)` equals their `(conn, corr)` (D-30). When refusals at the same offset must be told apart, add `and .record.rpc_id==<id>` to the query.
    - The hook side (`hook-invoked{hook_event:"user-prompt-submit"}` for an ordinary send, `hook-invoked{hook_event:"session-start"}` for a `/clear` confirmed by its new session or a `/compact` confirmed by its same session (verified CLI); `corr` null) joins by the wrapper's `instance` + `hook_event` + `timestamp` inside `run.confirm_window`. An unconfirmable send has no `run.confirm_window` and no hook side: its lines are one `send-issued` and one `send-confirmed{confirmed:false}` under the same `corr`, with no `send-refused`;

- **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs, so no file is both appended to and exclusively locked (a layout chosen while Windows, where that pair fails (rust-lang/rust#54118), was a target, and kept). - **[Links] A link `driver → driven` is recorded when a `send` or `answer` is issued from inside a wrapped session to another instance, or by an explicit `viola link <driver> <driven>`. `viola unlink` removes it.** A call counts as coming from inside a wrapped session when the calling process has `VIOLA_NAME` set. The CLI and the MCP server pass that name as `from` in the request `params`, and the driven instance's wrapper appends a `link` event to its `events.ndjson` only when that `driver → driven` pair is not already in its link set. Repeated sends and answers add no line, and an explicit `viola link` of an existing pair adds none and answers its held `since` with `already_linked: true` (§Standard Contracts, Instance snapshot), so `since` is the time of the first link after any `unlink`. `unlink` appends an `unlink` event. Links are events in the log. The link set in the snapshot is derived by replaying them. Rationale: the log stays the single source of truth for the link set as it is for everything else. Both are built: the driven instance's wrapper serves the `link` and `unlink` methods (`LinkSet::link` / `LinkSet::unlink`, sharing `driver_of`), sent by the verbs `viola link <driver> <driven> [--json]` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven> [--json]`, and records the implicit link itself. The driven wrapper's `LinkSet` (`src/run/links.rs`) records it on a `send` after the second wheel and running-turn reads and directly before `send-issued`, and on an `answer` once every refusal has passed and the response's kind matched the pending dialog, before the answer is taken. Five shapes of it stand: a refused `send` or `answer` records no link; a `from` equal to the wrapper's own name links nothing; the `link` line's `source` is `wrapper`; the record sits directly before `send-issued`, so a send that is issued and then reads `not-delivered` has linked; and a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`. A link that cannot be recorded is `-32603`, with nothing issued or the answer not taken. The set is restored from the log at every start.

A start that loses the placement to a concurrent first start re-hashes the copy that stands: an equal copy is reused and `outcome` reads `ok`; a different one is `PinError::HashMismatch`, `outcome` `pinned-hash-mismatch`, the file left as found. - **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused with `budget-paused` through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human keys are never blocked, and a running turn finishes. The pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`. `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is, and a plain `release` returns the wheel to `driver` without lifting a budget pause. `release --budget` is sent to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only, until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under `budget.json.lock`, at three points: at start, when a `send` arrives, and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of these points, and only then is `budget-gate` appended. So a snapshot can still read `budget_paused: true` after the reset, until a `send` arrives or a turn ends, and every surface that shows the snapshot inherits that. The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, including any override, to the instance snapshot, where `list` reads it. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `src/run/budget.rs`, one `BudgetGate` per wrapper, no thread and no timer): a window is crossed only when its `used_percentage` is known and at or above its threshold and its `resets_at` is known, parses as RFC 3339 and is later than now, so a window whose `resets_at` is `"unknown"`, unparseable or passed never pauses. With both windows crossed the refusal names `five-hour`.
 The `send` point sits after the text refusals and the first `human-typing` read and before the running-turn read, so the order is `control-character` → `empty-text` → `human-typing` → `budget-paused` → `turn-running` → the readiness gate's wait; the gate is read once per `send`, never again after that wait. `answer`, `wait`, `last`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` do not read the gate (read in the diff: its five product call sites; since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the root case `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`, `tests/cli_budget.rs`, drives `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under one closed gate, each giving the exit code and the document it gives under an open one; no case drives `hook.dialog` under a closed gate). An override covers both windows until its end and is dropped at the next point after that end. It does not outlive its wrapper: every start, a revived one included, evaluates from `budget.json` alone and restores none. `release --budget` with no pause standing records nothing. `budget-gate` is appended, and the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are rewritten, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, both before the evaluation returns; a record that cannot land is an error and the recorded state stays as it was. The thresholds are read once, at the wrapper's start, and no value of either switches the gate off. The gate is fail-open: no reading, an `"unknown"` figure, a passed or unparseable `resets_at`, an unreadable or refused `budget.json` and a bad threshold each leave it open or at its default. The decision takes the wall-clock instant as an argument (no clock seam). With figures missing, viola uses the newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age. With no reading at all it records `unknown` and does not block.
 The statusline is wrapped only for sessions started by `viola run`, through a per-session settings override that then runs the user's own statusline command unchanged. A reading is recorded only when the payload holds `rate_limits`. Rationale: the per-model weekly window is hidden (claude-code#91920), so thresholds are set low. The user's global statusline config is never touched, and a visible, conservative governor supports the "ordinary individual usage" posture.

- **Error sanitization and secret scan:** no `events` helper runs after every E2E test: that check is not built, replaced by the three surface witnesses (`tests/channel_error_bodies.rs`, `tests/cli_error_bodies.rs`, the MCP cases of `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`), the enumeration and the census of writers (`tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`), reading the check in `tests/support/events.rs`. The rules:
  - CLI `--json`, MCP `isError` and channel `error.data` contain no absolute path (drive letter, `/home/`, `/Users/`, the temp home prefix), no serde path and no `Caused by`
  - Under `--json` the `cli` catch site prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout and leaves stderr empty, witnessed by `cli_verbs_print_the_internal_error_document_under_json` (`tests/cli_wait_last.rs`) and `a_frame_verb_that_cannot_open_its_log_is_internal_error` (`tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`); without `--json` the line `error: internal error` stands byte for byte, and `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent there.
  - The check: `tests/support/events.rs` `error_body_hit` and `assert_error_body_clean`, classes `absolute-path`, `caused-by`, `serde-path` and `planted`, reporting place and class, never bytes; self-tested by `error_body_check_reads_each_class_as_a_hit` and `error_body_check_reports_no_byte_of_what_it_read` (`tests/cli_error_bodies.rs`).
  - `channel_error_bodies` and `cli_error_bodies` are `[[test]]` tables with `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`, each on the `ci` profile's 20 s kill line.
  - `cli_error_documents_of_a_loosened_socket_directory_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` (`tests/cli_error_bodies.rs`) holds the socket directory's error documents, `revive --json`'s among them; `assert_names_nothing` and `digit_runs` (`tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs`) hold its log lines free of path, pid and uid.
  - every -32603 is exactly `"internal error"` / `null`
  - No `-32603` is driven in a scanned home, and no failpoint or counted panic stands for one; the unit layer holds it (`answer_a_panicking_dispatch_is_internal_error_and_closes`, `links_set_method_an_append_that_fails_is_internal_with_the_set_unchanged`).
  - every `diagnostics/*` file and log contains no `Cookie` header and no stripped-var values
  - `diagnostics/` files are 0600
  - **Canary** (obs-plan §8, High-class verification): every integration and E2E input is synthetic, and every prompt, send text, tool `input`, dialog answer and statusline payload the tests feed embeds one fixed canary string, a constant in `tests/support`. The scan asserts that the canary never appears in any home-level `<home>/diagnostics/*.ndjson` line. It may appear in `events.ndjson` (contract payloads) and in `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson` only. The same scan runs in CI over `target/e2e-home/**`, the harness capture in `target/agent-run/` except `run --mutants`' `target/agent-run/chunk.diff` (repository source text, excluded from the scan and from the `harness-<os>` upload), and `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` before any upload (obs-plan §9 step order). A hit is reported as file, line, byte offset and pattern class, never the matched bytes.
  - `v1-47`'s "after every end-to-end test" reads "after each job's end-to-end run": `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` `"1"` on the job and `if: always()` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), the `viola-chaos-*` home out (`.andromeda/obs-plan-detail/ci-integration.md`).

- **Surfaces involved:** cli (`hook`)
- **Unparseable external values** become the string `"unknown"` in viola's own records, never an error. This covers `resets_at`, `used_percentage` and a missing statusline window.
- `viola list` holds the home to the read rule: `board::scan` reads it through `check_read` with or without an instance, so a 0750 home refuses the whole board (`ScanRefused::Home`).

- **Entity:** `viola run` TUI passthrough: the unmodified `claude` TUI hosted in openpty, entered by `viola run` and by a `viola revive` whose preflight passed (the same start; the boundary below binds both verbs, and under revive the clause read by a case of its own is that a passed revive writes no line of its own while the child holds the terminal, `tests/chaos_revive.rs`)
  - **Source:** Arch excerpt, Stack → portable-pty + vt100 ("viola does not own the rendered TUI content"). Tests excerpt, E2E driver → tui ("Tests never parse the rendered child screen for content"). Creator brief excerpt, A11y Anti-Patterns ("Viola parses no screen for content (R7)").
  - **Assertability:** boundary-only
  - **Reason:** The rendered content belongs to the vendor (`claude`) and is not traced. The assertion boundary is viola's wrapper:
    - viola writes zero bytes to the terminal except the child's output;
    - human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or delayed past the current atomic paste;
    - focus, mouse and resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) pass through and do not count as human editing; every other byte does.
    - under `viola revive --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal, and viola writes nothing past it.
    - a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel (`serve_drops_a_refused_peer_before_any_frame`, `channel_endpoint_answers_protocol_faults` the control).

**Design direction:**
The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is a control-tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks. Every session holds the same slot for its whole life, so the eye goes to where `builder` always is. - `wait` `{after?, timeout_ms?, from?}` → `{event:<ndjson event line>, cursor}`, where `cursor` is the end offset of that event's line, or `{timed_out:true}`. `after` and `timeout_ms` are each absent or a non-negative integer that fits `u64` (`null`, a negative, a fraction or a string is `-32602`, `data: null`); unknown fields are ignored. The start offset is `after`, else `events.ndjson`'s end read at the call; a line counts only when it STARTS at or after it. A pending dialog comes first: an `after`-less `wait`, or one whose `after` is at or before the pending dialog's line, returns that dialog at once. Only `turn-ended` · `question` · `permission` · `plan` · `session-end` · `dialog-expired` wake (`viola_core::EventKind::WAIT_WAKE`); the deadline is `now + timeout_ms` through `Instant::checked_add` (an unrepresentable instant is no deadline). The wake (`src/run/wait.rs` `WaitFeed`): one `Mutex` (a generation counter + the newest turn) and one `Condvar`; `WaitFeed::appending` runs each hook line's append inside the lock, then bumps the generation, keeps a `turn-ended` as the newest turn and wakes the parked calls. Hook lines signal, and of the wrapper's own records only `dialog-expired`, appended through `WaitFeed::appending` (the wrapper's `send-*`, `link`, `unlink` and start records never wake). A parked `wait` reads the generation before each scan, re-scans only when it moves, and its 20 ms `wait_timeout` re-reads the injected clock against the deadline, never the file; it holds its connection's worker thread until a wake, its deadline or the wrapper's exit.

It exits non-zero on any failing line and prints `file`, line number and the failing schema keyword, never the line's content (detail lines carry the canary). The check body and the JSON Schema validator crate are tests-owned; obs owns both schemas.

```sh
# G1: whole workspace from its root (root bin `viola` + crates/* + tests/ + fuzz/); target/ is skipped through .gitignore
set +e; rg -n -U --pcre2 --type rust '#\[(tracing::)?instrument\b(?!\(\s*skip_all\b)' .; test $? -eq 1
# G2: first fail if no home-level role file exists (an empty scope would pass vacuously); the start point ends in a slash, so a scope that is a link to a directory is descended (the Linux dev host's `target/e2e-home`; on a real directory the walk is the same); `awk 1` ends every file's last line with a newline; -R + fromjson? skip a torn line (not a panic record) instead of failing with jq exit 2
test -n "$(find target/e2e-home/ -path '*/diagnostics/*.ndjson' ! -name 'detail-*' -print -quit)"
find target/e2e-home/ -path '*/diagnostics/*.ndjson' ! -name 'detail-*' -exec awk 1 {} + | jq -R -n -e --arg seam src/cmd/hook/seam.rs '[inputs|fromjson?|select(.event=="panic")|select(((.panic_location|type)=="string" and (.panic_location|test(":[0-9]+$")) and ((.panic_location|sub(":[0-9]+$";""))==$seam))|not)]|length==0'
# G3: no abort panic strategy (profile `panic` key, `-C panic` rustflag, CARGO_PROFILE_*_PANIC env) in Cargo.toml, cargo config or workflows (§7); default regex engine; only rg exit 1 passes
set +e; rg -n --hidden -g 'Cargo.toml' -g 'config.toml' -g '*.yml' -g '*.yaml' "(panic|_PANIC)\s*[:=]\s*[\"']?abort" .; test $? -eq 1
```

```markdown
- **Format:** JSON-per-line. There are two streams:
  - **Event stream:** product events in `instances/<name>/events.ndjson`, exactly the arch Event line `{"v":1,"ts","instance","kind","source":"hook|wrapper|cli","data"}`.
  - **Process logs:** emitted by tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 `fmt().json().flatten_event(true).with_current_span(false)`, writing to `<home>/diagnostics/{run-<name>,hook-<name>,mcp,cli-<name>}.ndjson`. Files are 0600, dirs 0700, with one `write` per line.
- **Required fields:**
  - For process logs: `timestamp` (RFC 3339 UTC with ms and `Z`), `level` (`DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR`), `target`, and `fields.message` (or the flattened `message`).
  - `event`, a closed kebab-case enum. A new value needs a Decisions Log entry, like the §3 closed enums. Each value fixes what its `corr` holds:
    - `channel-request`, `channel-response`: `corr` = the JSON-RPC request `id`
    - `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered`: `corr` = `dialog_id`
    - `hook-invoked`, `hook-decision`: `corr` = `dialog_id` for dialog hooks, otherwise null
    - `send-issued`, `send-confirmed`, `send-refused`: `corr` = the send `cursor`
    - `process-start`, `process-exit`, `panic`: `corr` = null
  - `process` (`run|hook|mcp|cli`) and `instance` (a `ViolaName` or null).
  - `corr` is copied unchanged as a JSON number or string. It is never renamed (for example to `correlation_id`).

  obs-plan may add fields but must not rename or remove these. The harness greps on them.
- **Constraints:**
  - The hook trace is the `hook-<name>.ndjson` file. A failed write there is swallowed, so the hook still exits 0 and never writes to stderr.
  - No line may contain a `Cookie` header or any stripped `CLAUDE*` value. This is enforced by the secret-scan test in §6.
- **Agent parsing:** lines parseable with `jq -c 'select(.event=="dialog-raised")'` or equivalent; NEVER multi-line stack traces. A panic in a hook is caught and logged as one `level:"ERROR", event:"panic"` line.
```

- **Hint line:** directly under each refusal, `hint: <one plain instruction>`, keyed by reason (or by reason · detail). Exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes, and every cause gets its own hint, so an agent can tell the causes apart from the last stderr line (design-system cli pattern 2). The exit-1 start refusal `unable: <name> is already live` takes `hint: viola list`. `wait`, `last`, `link` and `unlink`'s exit 21 `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` (for `link` / `unlink`, `<name>` is the driven instance) takes `hint: <name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances` when the instance is not running (`viola send`'s exit 21 keeps its `[/ ] unable` mirror with the same hint). A frame verb's exit 21 on a name with no directory at its instance path takes `hint: <name> is not a wrapped session; only sessions started with viola run take commands`, and with its wrapper lost while the call is open `hint: <name>'s wrapper went away during the call; viola list shows whether it is still running`, each the last stderr line in plain ASCII. A frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) whose server check finds that the process on the endpoint is not the recorded wrapper, or cannot make the check, writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` with stderr empty. A frame verb meeting a refused socket directory writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` with stderr empty. There is no hint for the `unknown` refusal, whose detail is a code word or nothing, for `wrapper fault` or for `internal error`. A hint never quotes the sent text or any upstream text, and never names a path or a pid.

- **Bounded readers at every boundary.** Every product reader of external bytes is bounded in the same statement (`take`) or named in an `EXCEPTIONS` row; none reads an external byte source to its end unbounded. The E2E contract binary `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` (a `contract_` binary, run under `run --e2e`) holds it: its `BOUNDARIES` table, one `Boundary {` block per bounded read, names each read and its witness test, and `boundaries_each_name_a_bounded_read_that_stands` checks that each named read still stands; its `EXCEPTIONS` table names the own-executable reads, which are no external input. A census, `product_readers_are_each_bounded_or_named`, walks the product sources and judges each reader call bounded over its statement up to the call, matching an `EXCEPTIONS` needle against the call's whole source line, because the executable argument the needle names lies past the call's `(`; its self-check, `census_finds_an_unbounded_read_and_passes_a_bounded_one`, reads a planted unbounded read as a hit and passes a bounded one, and `serde_json_unbounded_depth_is_banned_in_deny_toml` reads the `deny.toml` feature ban. A new reader therefore lands bounded in its statement or as a named exception, or the census goes red.

  - **Entry point:**
    - One endpoint per `viola run`: socket file `<dir>/viola-<h12>.sock`, `<dir>` the per-user 0700 directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`) (§ Authentication & Authorization, IPC access control (Unix)).
    - Methods: `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `hook.dialog`, and `hook.event` notifications.
    - Whoever can connect can type prompts into the driven Claude session (`send`) and allow PermissionRequest dialogs (`answer` with `behavior:"allow"`). That amounts to running arbitrary tools, and so arbitrary code, as the user. They can also read the whole conversation (`wait`, `last`).
    - Whoever can connect can also add or remove a driver link (`link` / `unlink`), whose effect is a `link` / `unlink` line in `events.ndjson` and the snapshot's links only; neither method reads the self-reported `from`.
    - Sources: Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints); Cross-cutting Patterns (Local endpoint trust boundary).
  - **Trust boundary:**
    - v1 intends to trust every process of the same OS user and no other. How that is enforced (socket file mode, directory permissions) is not decided in arch and is explicitly handed to security.
    - There is no per-connection authentication. The `from` parameter is self-reported by the caller (the CLI and MCP take it from their own `VIOLA_NAME`), so link records and driver identity are not authenticated.
    - The endpoint name is predictable: FNV-1a over `ViolaName` + home path, which is not secret (Conventions: Endpoint name).
    - Consequences:
      - The socket sits in the per-user 0700 directory, not in world-writable `/tmp`.
      - A socket directory another user owns, a loosened one or a symlink is refused by the socket-directory check, with no bind on `run` and no frame on a client.
      - Clients (`hook`, `send`, `mcp`) connect to the `endpoint` recorded in the snapshot and act on whatever server answers there. A process holding that name while the real wrapper is gone could receive `hook.dialog` payloads and send back dialog decisions.
      - As built, every frame-writing client (CLI `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths; `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools) compares the connected peer's pid and that process's start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` before its first frame, and sends no frame on a mismatch or a check it cannot make. Each first runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`: the CLI verbs through `client::refuse_untrusted`, `viola hook` before its obs init, the `viola mcp` tools before `live_endpoint`), a refusal sending no frame, and then reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`, a replayed or absent snapshot giving no endpoint and so no frame; ahead of that comparison each runs the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint before connecting (a refusal `socket-dir-refused`, no frame) and the peer euid decision past the connect (a refusal `server-verify-failed`, no frame).
      - `run`'s exclusive bind means a squatted name blocks startup (exit 1).
    - Input validation is limited to JSON-RPC parsing, the `v` check (`-32602`) and the `ViolaName` nutype.
    - That limit is the wrapper's read of a frame. A client's read of the answer is screened on its own: `reply_of` and `of_reply` take a `refusal` or a string `detail` only as a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`) and a fault only through `viola_channel::sanitised_fault`, so nothing of the peer's but closed values reaches a CLI `--json` document or an MCP result; a code word outside the closed list stays visible by design.

Everything else in this set is **refused**: every other C0 control (U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, U+000E–U+001F, including ESC U+001B above all), DEL (U+007F) and every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F, including CSI U+009B). The check runs over decoded `char`s of the UTF-8 `&str`, never over raw bytes, because UTF-8 continuation bytes 0x80–0xBF are not C1 controls. This stops a bracketed-paste breakout through an embedded `ESC[201~`. **Reject, don't strip:** a text that holds a refused character is refused whole; no refused character is ever removed and the rest typed. **The typed text, an inner CR as one LF and the trailing CR and LF removed, allowed characters only:** after `validate_paste_text` has passed on the text as received, the wrapper's `send` takes the typed text once (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`: every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and every trailing CR and LF removed, in any order; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes, not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and from there on it is the only text `send` uses: the local-command classification (a listed local command followed by LF, CR or CRLF is that command: `/clear` and a CRLF is `/clear`), the in-flight text the delivery-confirmation exact match compares, `text_bytes` and the paste. A text that ends in CR, LF or CRLF and holds a refused character is still refused `control-character` with nothing typed.

- **[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.** `hook` blocks on the channel for a dialog answer. `wait` blocks until the next driver-relevant event (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` or `dialog-expired`) and returns that event, so nothing polls and a driver parked in `wait` learns that a dialog is pending. If a dialog is already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, it returns that dialog at once (as landed by 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: `hook.dialog` is served, the dialog line is appended and signalled through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` and cleared through `WaitFeed::dialog_settled`). With an `after` past that line the driver has already seen the dialog, so `wait` blocks for the next driver-relevant event, and a driver that leaves a dialog to the human never spins. Each dialog event carries a wrapper-assigned `dialog_id` (an integer, monotonic per instance, with the counter restored from `events.ndjson` on start so an id never repeats across wrapper restarts), and `answer` names its target by that id. At most one dialog is pending per instance. A `hook.dialog` that arrives while another is pending is answered `null` at once, so that dialog renders for the human. Its event is still logged with its own `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. Whether Claude Code can hold two dialog hooks open at once (for example on parallel tool calls) is a capability-ledger row. `wait` takes an optional `after` cursor and an optional `timeout_ms`. `after` is a byte offset into the instance's `events.ndjson`.
 `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it, at once if that event is already logged, so a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`, the offset to pass as the next `after`. Without `after`, `wait` returns the next such event appended after the call. With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until an event arrives, and if the endpoint vanishes first the caller gets `instance-unreachable`, its `detail` `endpoint-lost`. On timeout it returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}`. `last` returns the `last_assistant_message` of the newest `turn-ended` event. The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start. Endpoint names are a short hash of the instance, never the raw `VIOLA_NAME` + path. Rationale: one API over Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. Accepted risk: interprocess has one main maintainer, which the seam contains.

A counted, scoped or package object also carries `"host_excluded"` when at least one mutant was left out (step 4, Verdict): an array of `{"name","cfg"}`, the name cargo-mutants' own and the predicate as written in source, repo-relative and never an absolute path. The field is absent when nothing was left out.
  - The run document gains a top-level `"archived"` (after `mutants` in key order) whenever the run had a source to archive: the repo-relative `target/run-archive/<n>` holding the JUnit files this run's nextest or coverage suites wrote (`junit-{nextest-unit,nextest-integration,coverage}.xml`) and the `outcomes.json` its mutation arm read (`<n>` = the highest existing + 1; the newest 10 kept; gitignored, outside `target/agent-run/`, never uploaded). An absent source is skipped and named on stderr (`run-archive: skipped {name} (absent)`).
  - A document refused by a tool arm carries `"reason"` and, where one applies, `"detail"` (e.g. `tool-missing` + `cargo-fuzz`).
  - `skipped` counts only tests that were selected and then not run: JUnit `<skipped/>` entries (`#[ignore]`). Tests excluded by the layer filterset (for example `kind(test)` binaries during `nextest-unit`) and tests compiled out by an OS `#[cfg(…)]` gate are never counted, so the `gate` `suite-skipped` breach fires only on a real skip. The `doctest` suite has no JUnit. It is counted from the `test result: … N passed; M failed; K ignored` lines of `cargo test --workspace --doc`, with `ignored` as `skipped`, so doc examples that must not run use `no_run` or a `text` fence, never `ignore`.
  - Failing test names are listed in `suites[].failures[]`.
- **Stack traces** never print. Errors are fixed messages, and full detail goes only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/`.

_Included despite v1 auth approach "none". Threat Model Sec 6 elevates "IPC endpoint access control and server impersonation". Every principal check in viola is OS-level (IPC, filesystem). See the Security Decisions Log._
**Docker volumes, containers, service names:** none.
- _hook deadlines need performance-budget tests_

- NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `ledger/stamps.json` holds a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version. NEVER let any process other than `viola verify` write `ledger/stamps.json`. A stamp is what switches on dialog answering, including PermissionRequest `allow` (Threat Model Sec 1 config; architecture.md CLI Version Compatibility).
 The ledger has twenty-four rows (`LedgerRow::ALL`: the six spine rows, the four screen and timing rows, the four dialog-tier rows `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency`, the three framing rows `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear`, the newline row `paste-newline`, the three statusline rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits`, the resume row `resume-session`, the agents row `agents-join` and the compact row `local-command-compact`), and a stamp is read over the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, all twenty-four rows on every build, counter `/24`), so a non-`null` decision flows only when every relied row passes: a home stamped `20 pass  4 fail` records `cli_verified:false`, and so does a stamp holding exactly the fourteen older ids, or exactly the seventeen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, all `pass`, and one holding exactly the eighteen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows or exactly the twenty-one of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, or exactly the twenty-two of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, or exactly the twenty-three of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row; the hook prints nothing and `answer` exits 12 `unverified-cli`. The dated gap (R2, the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-04) under which decisions flowed on the ten-row stamp is closed.

- Exit `1` also covers `viola verify` refusing the home tree (`check_home_tree` with no name and no key: the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists), checked before its `cli` log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr, no step line, no summary and no log line. A strict-modes refusal from `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`) in its measuring step prints the same pair.

- **Files (`~/.viola/`):** Plaintext by design (Established Decisions: Database / State Store). Protected by OS permissions only:
  - 0700 directories and 0600 files, except the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola`, which is 0700.
  - The strict-modes check runs at startup (Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control).
  - **Code-bearing artefacts:**
    - `viola run` always rewrites `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`replace_private_shared`: a replace that fails counts as done only when the file already holds exactly the rendered bytes, which a concurrent start of the same version writes) rather than trusting an existing copy.
    - `instances/<name>/settings.json` (the per-session override whose statusline command Claude Code executes) is `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<pinned path> hook statusline"}}`. `viola run` rewrites it whole at every start, a revived start included, with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, 0600), after the first snapshot and before the spawn, and never reuses an existing copy. Its command uses the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` path (§ Universal). It is written only when every character of the pinned path is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :` (`viola_agent_claude::statusline::override_document`), since a shell runs the string unquoted; for any other path no override is written. The child gets `--settings <instance dir>/settings.json` after `--plugin-dir <dir>` and before the caller's arguments, only when an override was written. The flag is the agent crate's constant (`statusline::SETTINGS_FLAG`), which `viola verify`'s Runs C and D read too (moved at chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). **Ratified:** a code-bearing file written at every start and handed to the CLI is a boundary widening the founder ratified (live, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the operator).
    - `<hash>` is a truncated SHA-256 of the exe bytes (the first 16 hex characters of the digest). Before reusing an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola`, `viola run` re-hashes the file with SHA-256 and compares the truncated result with `<hash>`. On a mismatch it refuses to start (exit 1). The SHA-256 implementation is `sha2 =0.11.0` with `default-features = false` (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`): pure Rust, no `cc` on the one `[graph]` triple (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`), passing the cargo-deny C-build ban; `tests/contract_content_hash.rs` pins it against published FIPS 180-2 vectors and the 16-hex truncation. A non-cryptographic fallback is banned (§ Data Protection). Because the hash is cryptographic, this catches substitution as well as accidental corruption. Tampering by the same OS user (who could also rewrite the folder name) stays outside the v1 boundary.
    - `viola run`'s start pins the bytes it has already checked (`viola_state::pin::pin_bytes`, under the key `pin::pin_key`: `<VERSION>-<16 hex>`); `pin_exe`, which `viola verify` calls, delegates to `pin_bytes`. An absent copy is placed, never replaced, a copy another start placed first is re-hashed before reuse, and one tree's release builds can key two folders (each in the groups below).
    - `ledger/stamps.json` is written only by `viola verify`, under its `.lock`, with 0600.
    - `marketplace/` is written only by `viola plugin install`: two manifests and `viola/.mcp.json`, whose `mcpServers.viola` `command` is the canonical exe that ran the install and whose `args` are `["--home", <the canonical home>, "mcp"]`, built by `serde_json`, no hooks in any document; each file rewritten whole at 0600 on every run (`replace_private`), each dir 0700, any other entry left as found. Claude Code runs that command for MCP in a session that installed the plugin. viola never reads the tree back nor re-hashes the command, spawns no `claude` and writes nothing under `~/.claude`: the user runs the two printed `claude plugin` commands.
  - **Probe captures:** `viola verify` writes its probe plugin and the hook-payload captures under `ledger/probes/<pid>/` (0700). The captures, `captures/<Event>.<k>.json` claimed exclusively by the hidden `hook --capture` arm, are transient, content-bearing 0600 files, and so are Run B's status line captures under `typed/statusline/` (0700; `StatusLine.<k>.json` and its `StatusLine.<k>.shell` verdict, claimed by the hidden statusline capture arm) beside the 0600 probe settings `typed/statusline.json`; the `questions/` (Run C) and `plan/` (Run D) roots each hold their own `plugin/`, `captures/` and an `answers/` dir of compiled `ProbeAnswer` ids; the `resume/` root (Run E) holds the same capture plugin as `typed/` and its own `captures/`, read by the `resume-session` check and `ledger::resume_variants`; a drop guard removes the whole probe dir when `verify` passes, fails or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (only this run's `<pid>` dir), and only a scrubbed `--record` copy leaves it; SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leave it to be removed by hand.
  - **Interactive probe dirs (outside the viola home):** Run A's fresh `viola-verify-*` dir under the OS temp root, and in the user's current folder Run B's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`, Run C's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/`, Run D's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/`, which holds a 0700 `plans/` (its `plansDirectory`), and Run E's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/`. All are 0700 and removed when verify passes, fails, or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (a drop guard each; the repo's `.gitignore` carries `/.viola-verify-*/` for a leftover). The stop is `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` (`cmd::verify::stop`, installed by `viola verify` alone; its handler only sets one flag every wait reads). A stopped run kills and reaps its child with no key, and its guards remove only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing; it adds no owner record and no remover of an earlier run's or another process's dirs. SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install (ignored, fail-open) keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand: the founder's narrow entry (relayed by the overseer, 2026-10-10), and the event set the operator's P4 answer (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). Run C's one `allow` runs `touch viola-probe-permission` inside its own dir; Run D's plan file lands inside its own dir, never under `~/.claude/plans` (as measured on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287: `~/.claude/plans/` 17 → 17 files across the re-run). These are the founder's live rulings on the dirs (2026-10-05 08:25Z) and on M7 = A and STOP 7 (2026-10-05), relayed by the overseer.
- **Surfaces involved:** cli (`viola send` readback mirror `[RB]`).

- **CLI, `viola run` / `viola revive` start, strict-modes:** a home tree that fails the strict-modes check (the home, the instance's files, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, the pinned copy and its plugin folders) is refused with exit 1 before any log opens, no line written and no child started: the fixed home-state `unable` / `hint:` pair for a home-level refusal, the instance-state pair for an instance-level one, `hint:` last on stderr, stdout empty; under `--json`, `revive` gives its `strict-modes-failed` document (above).

- **The supply-chain advisories:** the Supply-chain stage's `supply-chain` job reads green with no advisory ignored: `deny.toml` `[advisories]` reads `ignore = []`, and `portable-pty` `=0.9.0` (through `nix 0.28.0`) puts no `pin-utils` in the graph (`cargo tree -i pin-utils` exit 101, no package), as measured at ci#42288148289.

**Rationale:** All eight values come from the exploration's Color World: the tower cab strip bay at night. The palette is a monochrome ladder of three surfaces (#1E2124 → #2A2E33 → #4A5057) and three inks (#E6D8AE, #9C9278, #3B3A36). Two hues are allowed, each locked to one role:

- **Level:** Performance / Load
  - **Coverage focus:** Budget assertions on perf-critical paths
  - **Tier-specific depth (Comprehensive, viola):** Required (performance-budget trigger present). hyperfine 1.20.0 gates the hook deadlines on `max` (the `--perf` arm, the five hyperfine rows — `pre-tool-use` included, on an unstamped perf session — and the `perf` CI job, on its one `ubuntu-latest` leg, are built; §10). The heartbeat staleness flip at >5 s is checked by `viola_state::liveness::classify`, a pure function fed the beat's age (no clock).

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh boot [--session <id>] [--instance <name>[:<fake-agent-args>]]... [--unstamped] [--cli-version <ver>] [--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed] [--statusline-echo]`. With no `--instance` flag, the instances are `overseer` and `builder`, whatever other flags are given (for example Path 6's `--statusline-echo`). One or more `--instance` flags replace that default list. `--agents-mode` defaults to `recorded`. `--statusline-echo` (built at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs; clap `conflicts_with` `--unstamped`, the misuse usage `arguments`: the home exists only once step 4's `viola verify` made it) runs after step 4 and before step 5. It configures the user statusline command as `<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent statusline-echo <home>/fake/statusline.marker`, both paths with forward slashes, in the settings source that `run` reads, redirected into the session home: it writes `<home>/statusline-source.json` (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, 0600, the settings shape `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":…}}`), which viola only reads and which is the source whenever it exists, and makes `<home>/fake/` through `create_private_dir`. A bin dir or home holding a character outside ASCII letters, digits and `_ - . / :` fails boot `reason:"build-failed"`. It sets no env var and writes no `budget.json`. It is used by Path 6 (§6 Path 6 step 1, `crates/viola-e2e/tests/path6_budget_harness.rs`). A `reason:"statusline-source-unresolved"` refusal is dropped: its premise (an unnamed source) is gone, and no entry owes it. `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` (built at the same chunk; an unknown value is usage `arguments`) writes the fake agent's `agents-mode` file beside the session's `bin/claude` copy, which the fake reads beside its exe; it sets no env var (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`). A stale file is removed before step 4 and the value written (`replace_private`, 0600) after step 4 and the statusline plant, before `supervise.json`: step 4's Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that same copy, so a mode written first failed the `agents-join` row (`verify-failed`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs under `malformed`). It is recorded as `agents_mode` (serde default) in `session.json` and `supervise.json`, so a spec can reproduce the E1 unwrapped row. Steps:
  1. `cargo build --workspace --features viola/fake-agent` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace root>/target/harness`. It never builds into the `target/` that the shim's `cargo run` uses: on the retired Windows host a running `target/debug/viola-harness.exe` could not be relinked, and a workspace-wide build re-fingerprints it (measured 2026-09-24: `os error 5`, `UnitDependencyInfoChanged`). On failure it reports `reason:"build-failed"`, and no timeout applies to this step.
  2. Choose the home under the workspace's `target/e2e-home/` (obs-plan §9: CI's zero-panic G2 gate, the G4 schema gate, the secret scan and the `diag-<os>` upload all read `target/e2e-home/**`). Create a unique parent with `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix("viola-session-").tempdir_in("<workspace root>/target/e2e-home")?.keep()` and pass `<parent>/home`, which does **not** exist yet, as `--home`. viola then creates the home itself, 0700. The base `target/e2e-home` itself is prepared before the `tempdir_in` by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`): a plain base (absent, or a directory) is created as a directory; on Unix a base that is a link must have an absolute target, which is made with mode 0700 when it is gone (one non-recursive create, never a chmod after, never a parent) and accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`; the message and the floor: §3 Test data bootstrap). A refused base reads `reason:"build-failed"`, the reason a failed create gave before; none was added. On the Linux dev host the base is an operator-set link to the owner-only tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` (§5 Setup / teardown lifecycle); the path string is unchanged, and no CI runner has a link.
  3. Copy `<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent` (see step 5) to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude`, and put that dir first on a harness-scoped `PATH`, passed per child via `Command::env` and never `set_var`. It serves both `viola verify` and the `claude agents --json` stub.
  4. Unless `--unstamped` is given, run `viola verify --home <home>` against the fake agent driven with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, so its print probe and all five interactive runs (Run A, Run B with its five added compiled pastes — the long, the tag-like and the newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear` — the dialog Runs C and D, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session) stamp every relied ledger row (`LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-four), Run B also making its one `claude agents --json` read (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) and carrying on Unix its one probe `--settings` (`typed/statusline.json`), whose status line the hidden `hook statusline --capture` arm files (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relayed verbatim by the operator). This requires exit 0 and a last stdout line matching `^stamped \S+  \d+ pass  0 fail$`. It is the only writer of `ledger/stamps.json`; see Decisions Log.
  5. Spawn the supervisor `viola-harness supervise --session <id>` as an ordinary child process (no detach flags; it outlives `boot` and stops only through `stop.request`). It owns one portable-pty (`=0.9.0`, via the `viola-pty` seam) outer PTY per instance — a master writer, the child and a drain thread — and runs `viola run <name> --home <home> -- <bin dir>/viola-fake-agent --cli-version <ver> --fixtures <workspace root>/fixtures/claude --receipt <home>/fake/<name>.receipt.ndjson --control <home>/fake/<name>.control --screens --trusted-root <cwd> <fake-agent-args>`, so a booted wrapper shows the trusted ready screen, where `viola` is also taken from `<bin dir>`. `--fixtures` names the parent dir: the fake agent joins `<cli-version>` itself, so replay follows `--cli-version` even under `--report-version`. `--plugin-dir` is not passed by the harness: `viola run` passes it to the child (architecture §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names). It drains every master on its own thread. `<bin dir>` is the directory boot step 3 copies from: `target/harness/debug` (boot step 1's target dir) for the CLI, the test executable's own target dir for `harness_session`, and `target/perf/release` for `--perf`. The harness never reads `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`, because Cargo sets that only for the root package's own integration tests. `<workspace root>` is resolved from `cargo metadata` or `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` and passed as an absolute path, because nextest runs `viola-e2e` tests with `crates/viola-e2e` as the cwd. The control file is created empty before spawn. Both rstest `booted_wrapper` copies pass the same `--control` path.

- `Launch` carries `json: bool` (`run` passes false, `revive` passes `args.json`). With it true, `refused_with` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) prints `refused_document` in place of the human pair for `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name` and `socket-dir-refused`, and a program not found, which has no human pair, prints `internal-error`; each returns before `spawn_child`.

**Vector:** CLI arguments, flags and environment: `--home` and `VIOLA_DIR` choose which state tree, snapshot, `endpoint`, `statusline_command` and ledger stamps are used; the trust boundary is same-user invocation, clap parsing, the `ViolaName` nutype and tolerant `config.json` parsing.

- `--coverage` replaces the nextest invocations of steps 1+2 with `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci --lcov --output-path target/lcov.info --ignore-filename-regex '(viola-fake-agent|crates[/\\]viola-e2e|tests[/\\]support|fuzz[/\\])' --fail-under-lines 85 --fail-under-functions 95 --fail-under-regions 80` (a `--filter` passes as `-E`). The regex is the harness const `COVERAGE_IGNORE`: the same four trees, separator-agnostic, a form kept from the Windows target, where llvm-cov reports paths with `\`. That run reports as the single suite `coverage` (JUnit copied as `junit-coverage.xml`, see `gate`). Then `cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only` writes `target/agent-run/artifacts/llvm-cov-summary.json`. The suite's failure codes are `llvm-cov-exit-N` (a red exit over green tests, e.g. a floor breach) and `llvm-cov-summary-missing`. The `cargo test --workspace --doc` run from step 1 still follows it, as suite `doctest`. llvm-cov builds in its own target dir, so no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set.
- **Truncation:** only unwrapped NAMEs, with `...`, and only where the terminal width is known. Wrapped names are never clipped. No line ever wraps.

- NEVER rely on the socket file's 0600 mode as the only Unix control: `unix(7)` says socket permissions may be ignored. NEVER set it with `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`: a rule set while macOS (where it returns `Unsupported` and fails the bind) was a target, and kept; chmod after the bind instead.

- **Vector:** The human's terminal, `viola run`'s own stdin.
  - **Entry point:** Every byte the terminal writes to `viola run`'s stdin: the human's keys, and the terminal's own focus reports, mouse reports and replies to the child's queries. A byte that is typing takes the wheel from the driver (`wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}`), and the next automation `send` is refused `human-typing` (Established Decisions: Human Takeover / Wheel).
  - **Trust boundary:** The stdin classifier's closed non-editing list (the founder's ruling F-W2): only a sequence on it never counts as typing, and every other byte does. The list was widened once, a boundary widening ratified by the founder himself on 2026-10-08 after the exact grammars and a narrower option of two were shown (relayed verbatim by the overseer; chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive): seven terminal reply shapes after `CSI`, each by exact grammar, the fields compared as bytes, no intermediate byte and the field count exact (`0 n`, `? 997;1 n` and `? 997;2 n`, `4;n;n t`, `6;n;n t`, `8;n;n t`, `48;n;n;n;n t`, `> 4;n m`), as measured on foot 1.28.0 on the Linux dev host, where those replies had taken the wheel from the driver at a live session's start. The nearest human keys (`n`, `t`, `m`, their Alt forms, their kitty key events) and a sequence one field or one prefix away stay typing, each pinned by a unit case, and a reply no terminal has been measured to write is never added on a guess. The classifier reads bytes, not time: a human who types a listed reply's bytes one key at a time is read as that reply. A key that reaches this stdin is the human's by construction, whoever typed it: at the same chunk an agent typed five keys into session terminals with `wtype`, each on a compositor the chunk started itself (nested as one client window of the locked desktop's compositor, one start for all live work) and each after a guard read that its one window was the active one. That crossing of the human's own input is the founder's ruling for that chunk's takeover proof (his answers of 2026-10-08, the method first, then the compositor's form and its price after they were shown, relayed verbatim by the overseer): the desktop's lock was never touched and read locked after the start, before each live step and twice after the end, the one call naming the desktop instance was a `locked` read, and no product code took part.

- **Definition:** zero tolerance on three counts: 0 `event:"panic"` lines in any CI artifact (as G2 counts them: the `fake-agent` seam's deliberate panic at exactly `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs:<digits>` excepted, §9), 0 secret-scan hits, 0 schema-conformance failures.

- **Verification, one hint per code:** in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`, `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, with its control `shared_hints_reads_a_planted_duplicate`, holds each code to its own hint, and `no_hint_names_release` holds every hint from naming `release`.
