body: - NEVER parse the rendered `claude` TUI beyond its compiled input-box and modal signatures, or take screenshots as a11y evidence (R7).

- Env vars: `VIOLA_` prefix (`VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_BIN`) — wrapper-to-child plumbing only, never configuration. Test-harness-only variables use `AGENT_RUN_` (`AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` — read by `viola-harness`, the root test chain `tests/support/home.rs` and/or viola-e2e's `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` `Booted` guard and `harness::session` guard (`HarnessSession`'s `Drop`, through `keep_home`, which reads both `KEEP_*` variables) and are never read by `viola`. Besides `PATH` (read and set for the child) and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (read only, for the socket directory), two of the ratified exceptions are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (u64 ms capped at 5 000; security-plan Decisions Log 2026-09-27) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (fires only on exactly `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic; Decisions Log 2026-09-28), neither prefix: each read only by a `viola` built with the `fake-agent` feature, absent from release builds, configuring nothing. A third, in every build: `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, the terminal's own names, read (never set) only by viola's colour layer (`src/human/style.rs`, `viola list`'s human mode) to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written — never echoed, configuring nothing, disabling no control and widening no redaction (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline; arch §Occupied Resources → Environment variables).

- Timestamps: `ts` on every instance event and the `hook.event` frame (request frames carry no instant), `timestamp` on process-log and detail lines, `*_at` for other instants (a link record's start instant excepted); RFC 3339 UTC with ms and `Z` (`to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Millis, true)`).

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 budget-paused · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed words `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened; and `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created, no log opened; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; and, on those same eight verbs, past that check and before any connect, a refused socket directory on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir` in `client::connect`): the socket-directory hint last on stderr, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` under `--json`, one `process-exit` at WARN with `during` `connect` and no `channel-request`); `viola hook` always 0. `viola revive` exits 0, 1 for a refused strict-modes check (ahead of the wrapper log: the stderr pair, no log line) or a preflight refusal (`already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`, read in that order, each one `process-exit` line) or a refusal of the start after a passed preflight, or 2 for a usage error; it takes `--json` on both arms, where a refused strict-modes check and every refusal of its start is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, by `client::refused_document`; a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start is `internal-error`), stderr empty, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order (a `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal).

- `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`; keys: the budget thresholds `five_hour` / `seven_day` (whole numbers into `Percent`, defaults 90 / 85, read once at the wrapper's start and by `viola list` at each run; a bad value takes that key's default with one `parse-rejected` line per key, and no value switches the gate off), `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`; the only source of the process-log level, `RUST_LOG` having no effect; obs D-15), `claude_env_keep` (the R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty; a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect), `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start; any other value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected` line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded).

**What breaks:** exact-match delivery confirmation fails on long pastes (wrapped in `<pasted_content id=…>` above ~981 bytes on 2.1.280) and on tag-like text (`<` becomes `<\`).
**How to avoid:** `viola-agent-claude` classifies `harness` on the raw prefix first, then removes the wrapper with its frame, then reverses tag escaping, before emitting `prompt-submitted`.
**References:** arch Ledger rows; test-plan Path 2 step 3.

The only crate that knows Claude Code. It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses the statusline `rate_limits` and, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- Listener: 0700 per-user dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`, never the `/tmp` root) checked before bind and before connect by `viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir` (one `symlink_metadata`; an absent path passes; a symlink, a non-directory, another owner, any group or other bit or an unstattable path is refused, `socket-dir-refused`, left as found and never chmodded), never inside `viola_channel::Client::connect`: `viola-channel` has no `viola-state` edge, so the check stands at the channel seam's callers; socket chmod 0600 after the bind (never `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`); `.lock` sibling as the start arbiter; `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))` (`peer_creds` euid), so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file and writing no line; `Server::serve` injects `peer_admitted` as a `type Admission` through the private `serve_admitting`, with no env, flag or feature seam. `try_overwrite` off.

- stdout carries MCP frames only; logs go to `<home>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` (if the file cannot be opened it exits 1 and prints nothing) once its home and `diagnostics/` (each that exists) pass `viola_state::strict::check_path`; a refusal exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file, and does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs that server's connection as failed (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host). The `rmcp` log target is OFF. After a session a stdin line past `MAX_FRAME` ended, `viola_mcp::serve` writes exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` at WARN through `obs_event!`, holding no byte of the line, then returns what the session gave: `Ok(())` once the session initialized (exit 0, as at a closed stdin), or `ServeError::Initialize` (exit 1, both streams empty; 11 is only the unit child's own code, `serve_child_entry`) when the cut lands before `initialize` completes.

- Licence: the project is `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (`[workspace.package]`, `license.workspace = true`; `LICENSE-MIT` + `LICENSE-APACHE`). `deny.toml` allows `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `Zlib`, `Unicode-3.0`, plus `0BSD` only through the per-crate exception for interprocess's `doctest-file`, never through the allowlist.

- **Wrapper:** `src/run/` (pump, wheel, governor, gate wiring; `gate.rs` the bounded feed + `Gate`; `agents.rs` the bounded `claude agents --json` read (`read_logged`, `read_here`) shared by `list`, `revive`, verify's Run B and the `mcp` `list` tool (through `list::board_document`); `send.rs` the `send` module root — the `send` method on `Ctx` with its refusal order, re-exporting `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` and `parse_from` —, one in flight with the remembered session id, the text validated as received and then typed with every inner CR or CR LF as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF (`typed_text`, the one text the list, the match, `text_bytes` and the paste read; an empty typed text is refused `empty-text` before the first wheel read, and by the client's `refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs` before any frame), and its phases under `send/`: `slot.rs` the one-in-flight `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` with the driver relabel and the `session-start` post-condition claim; `classify.rs` the local-command decision over `LOCAL_COMMANDS` (`classify`); `params.rs` `parse` / `parse_from`; `budget.rs` `Ctx::budget_paused`; and beside `send.rs` in `src/run/`: `wait.rs` the `WaitFeed` — the append under its lock, the Condvar wake, the newest turn and its start rebuild (which also returns the highest `dialog_id`), `appending_dialog` / `dialog_settled` — and the `wait` / `last` methods; `dialog.rs` the `DialogSlot` — the `hook.dialog` and `answer` methods, one pending dialog, the Condvar await on the injected clock up to the instance's dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, a `DialogHold` of whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start through `run::dialog::read_hold` right after the thresholds), at whose end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line (`{dialog_id, dialog_kind}`, `source: wrapper`) through `WaitFeed::appending`, waking a parked `wait`, the per-tool armed continuation matched on equal `tool_input`; `wheel.rs` the `WheelSlot` — holder + cause under one lock, the synchronous in-memory move, the record worker (the `wheel` event, the snapshot, `run.wheel_transition`, the pending-dialog hand-back) flushed ≤ 2 s at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode, the stdin observer `Observed` and the F-W2 `Classifier`, and the `pause` / `release` methods; `snapshot.rs` the `Snapshots` holder every snapshot write goes through)

- `{"v":1,"ts":"<RFC3339 ms Z>","instance":"<ViolaName>","kind":"<kind>","source":"hook|wrapper","data":{}}` — one complete object + `\n` per single `write` call; multi-line text travels as an escaped string.

- Colour decision order (first match → no colour): `--json` · `viola run` · `viola hook`/`mcp` · `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included) · `TERM=dumb` · non-TTY stdout. SGR only for amber `DIALOG`, dim `stale` rows, bold NAME — always beside its word; never on `unable` / `fail`. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), `list` is uncoloured under any rung above; on a terminal that takes colour every NAME value is bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog takes the attention token (its kind word plain), a wrapped `stale` row is dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, the spans are laid over the escaped, padded cells (the plain board's columns, one write), and the depth is truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM` (`COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read). A wrapped row joined to one `claude agents --json` read by child pid or agent session id reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; each unjoined session follows under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME its `sessionId`, LIVE `live`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, with no separator when there is none and the board as with no `claude` on a failed read. With the terminal's width known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME longer than its column (capped at the width less 65) is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...`, never inside an escape; a wrapped NAME is never cut, and a piped board or `--json` keeps every name whole.

- A new listener or channel method needs a Security Decisions Log entry first. CLI `--json` documents, MCP error results and channel error data carry codes and fixed messages only, no path, pid or upstream text; `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` enumerates every error body with its writer and witness (`CLI_DOCUMENTS`, `MCP_RESULTS`, `CHANNEL_FAULTS`, with `NOT_ERROR_BODIES` and `PLUMBING` the named exclusions), and `product_error_writers_are_each_named` fails on an unnamed product error writer and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` on an interpolating `thiserror` message. Every exit-21 cause and exit-1 code passes `is_code_word` and is a row of that binary, carrying no path, pid or upstream text; `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` holds the exit-21 and exit-1 cause table (`every_code_is_a_code_word`, `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `no_hint_names_release`).

- Success: `isError:false` + the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent`; refusal, unreachable, fault or invalid params: `isError:true` + codes only, text `refused: <code>`; `instance-unreachable` carries its cause in `detail` through `result::unreachable(cause)`: `of_reply` reads `Connect` as `instance-dead` and `Closed | Io` as `endpoint-lost`, `of_board` the board's refusal as `strict-modes-failed`, and `tools.rs` `frame` a refused `check_instance` as `strict-modes-failed`, no `live_endpoint` by `without_endpoint`, a refused `check_endpoint_dir` after `live_endpoint` as `socket-dir-refused` and a refused `peer_admitted` or a failed `server_verified` as `server-verify-failed`, `isError` the only record; JSON-RPC errors are only the connection's own faults, an unknown tool (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault (`-32603` `internal error`, `data: null`); `tools/list` and `server/discover` each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (claude 2.1.287 drops every tool without them). rmcp features exactly `server` + `transport-io`; `viola mcp`'s stdin reaches rmcp only through `viola_mcp::stdin::CappedLines` at `MAX_FRAME` per line (rmcp reads stdio lines unbounded), an over-long line refused whole, never truncated or skipped, and ending the session as a closed stdin does; every call returns below the client's tool-call timeout: MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, 50 000)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`), 50 000 ms when none is given, below claude 2.1.287's stdio tool-call default (over 50 s, as measured live).

- `viola verify [--record <dir>] [-- <program> [args…]]` — drive one print-mode probe (Haiku) and five interactive PTY runs (Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` (for shell-plain paths, also one probe `--settings <probe dir>/typed/statusline.json` whose status line the hidden `hook statusline --capture` arm files) with six compiled pastes (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a 113-byte text holding one inner LF, `/compact`, `/clear`) and one `claude agents --json` read once its first turn has settled, before the five added pastes (held in memory, spawn pair `agents-probe`, no start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E in `-resume/` resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (input empty, no `--settings`); no key into any dialog — the probe hook answers C and D's) against the CLI (default `claude`), check the relied ledger rows (`LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-four, on every build), print `[NN/MM]` step lines (`MM` the relied count, 24; the last `[24/24] local-command-compact …`) + the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary on stdout and write `ledger/stamps.json`; exit 1 on a failing row; exit 1 with the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary and no log line when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens (and the same pair, exit 1, after the step lines, when `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`, with `detail:"strict-modes-failed"` on its `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`); a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM kills its child with no key, removes only the probe dirs it created, writes no stamp, leaves stdout empty, prints `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` and exits 1 (SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leaves the dirs to remove by hand). `--record <dir>` also writes the scrubbed `<dir>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants, Run B's `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants, Run B's status line variants `StatusLine.default-1.json` / `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json`, Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json`, Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only) and signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens when 0 rows fail; an unclean recording is refused naming the file and check code. Run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is answered. Against the real CLI: local only, spends tokens; CI runs it only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode and its `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing` interactive modes. The `Mcp.<variant>.json` MCP exchanges are recorded not by `--record` but by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`, the same scrub and closed refusal codes; architecture §Occupied Resources → Binary)

**"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `not-delivered`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (on a verified CLI, for `/clear` until its new-session post-condition does and for `/compact` until its same-session compact post-condition does; on an unverified CLI both `/clear` and `/compact` stay `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`, and old information carries its age (`read 4m ago`, `expired`). It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.

- Refusal lines — `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>` on stderr, then the cause's `hint:` line last; the exit-1 refusals of `run`, `revive` and `verify` and every exit-21 strict-modes refusal use the fixed `unable: <text>` / `hint:` pair instead

- **`viola-agent-claude`** — the only crate that knows Claude: hook parsing, dialog mapping, R8 strip, child program resolution, capability ledger, the vt100 screen model and readiness verdict, the pure `agents` module (the `claude agents --json` parse into rows or the closed `AgentsFailure`), the resume argument shapes (`--resume`, `--fork-session`, the session-id shape), the pure `statusline` module (the payload reading, the settings reader, the `--settings` override document and `viola verify`'s probe document, the `/bin/sh -c` argv), the pure `marketplace` module (`plugin install`'s three documents, `NAME`, `PLUGIN_REF`)

- No `config.json` key, `VIOLA_*` env var or CLI flag may disable a control or widen redaction; env vars are not a configuration channel (no `RUST_LOG`, `EnvFilter` or `OTEL_*`; outside `VIOLA_*` plumbing a build reads only the `fake-agent` test seams, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (the socket directory) and `PATH` (program lookup) and, in every build, `NO_COLOR` / `TERM` / `COLORTERM`, by `viola list`'s human mode only to choose its SGR bytes); never add an env, flag or feature seam to force a refusing peer-euid decision: the decisions are proven over injected values.

- Disk state: set 0700 dirs / 0600 files explicitly (never the umask; the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` copy is 0700), and never chmod a refused socket directory: it is left as found, never narrowed; only the wrapper writes `snapshot.json`, only `viola verify` writes `ledger/stamps.json`; one `write` per ndjson line; never truncate `events.ndjson`.

viola is mechanism, not policy: it carries typed input, answers dialogs when told to, logs everything and holds the wheel, but never decides what to answer — driver-side policy (Andromeda's decision rights included) stays outside the binary. Every behaviour of the `claude` CLI it relies on is a measured, version-stamped capability-ledger row; on an unverified CLI build viola degrades to transport-only and every send is confirmed after the fact (`prompt-submitted` read-back or a ledger post-condition), never presumed, the one exception a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is none or not yet measured, or whose CLI is unverified: `ok` with `confirmed: false`, detail `unconfirmable`.

- **Log sink path:** codes-only role files `<home>/diagnostics/{run-<name>,hook-<name>,mcp,cli-<name>}.ndjson` (`mcp` always writes `mcp.ndjson`, its home and `diagnostics/` checked by strict-modes before the sink opens; no stderr fallback: a file that cannot be opened exits 1 printing nothing); every role or detail file opens only past `check_diagnostics` on the existing `diagnostics/` folder and the file (a symlink, or a folder or file another user may read, is refused as a failed open: the role writer a sink, the detail line dropped); content-bearing detail `<home>/instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson`; 0600 in 0700

- `mutants.out/` is never uploaded; it stays at the repository root (gitignored); on the Linux dev host a directory named `viola-mutants-scratch/` is only the operator's NOCOW `TMPDIR`, printed by no document either. `target/run-archive/<n>/` (each run's JUnit and the `outcomes.json` it read) is never uploaded either — gitignored, outside every upload path (obs-plan §8 item 5); the mutation run's `chunk.diff` at the harness capture root is excluded from the harness upload, so it is never scanned and never uploaded

- The statusline arm (as landed, chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through): `viola hook statusline` runs its instance check before obs init, because the role-file open sets an existing home to 0700; a refused check opens no role file and writes no line (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, superseding the operator's answer). Its lines: `hook-invoked`, `parse-rejected{parser:"hook-stdin"}` on rejected stdin, the `statusline-shell` `process-start` / `process-exit` pair only when the snapshot records a `statusline_command`, `hook-decision{budget_written, duration_ms}` with `detail` ∈ `oversize-stdin|malformed-json|deadline` (three of the six fail-open codes) and `deadline_hit` only when true. The hidden `hook statusline --capture` arm (`viola verify`'s Run B probe capture) does no obs init and runs no instance check, no shell-out and no `budget.json` write: it opens no role file, writes no line and prints nothing (panic exemption 5, with `hook <event> --capture`). Its stdout is the user's status-line output, never telemetry; the `max < 1.0 s` hook budget excludes it (its own bound is 5 s, PROVISIONAL). At start, the statusline source read and the settings override write carry no span and no line, by design.

- **Audit tool:** `cargo deny check` (>=0.20.2: advisories, bans, licences — `allow` exactly MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, `0BSD` only as the per-crate `[[licenses.exceptions]]` for interprocess's `doctest-file` (the one 0BSD crate in the Linux graph), a new exception needs a Decisions Log entry — sources — crates.io only; no advisory is ignored (`ignore = []`; portable-pty pinned `=0.9.0`)); the tokio ban is `deny-sync.toml`, run per sync crate as sole root over the four crates of `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, and for `viola-channel` (its Tokio client behind its `tokio` feature) the `cargo tree` form `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` (no `tokio v` line without the feature); `scripts/deny-probes.sh` proves every ban fires; weekly `cargo deny check advisories` in `nightly.yml` over the root and fuzz lockfiles; `zizmor` on workflows. Never widen an ignore, add a `skip`/`allow` or silence zizmor to reach green; the one admitted ignore is the Critical CVE response: within 7 days of an advisory confined to a disabled feature, an ignore entry whose reason names that feature (an advisory against an enabled feature: bump the crate within 7 days).

- Actions pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment, never a mutable ref, `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false`; workflow `permissions: {}`, job `contents: read`; no `rust-cache` in a release workflow.

- The only env vars outside `VIOLA_*` any `viola` build reads are `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (read by the channel endpoint only to place the socket directory), the terminal colour facts `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM` (every build, `viola list`'s human mode only, only compared and never echoed, deciding only whether and how deep SGR bytes are written; they reach no log line, error or refusal, configure nothing, disable no control and widen no redaction; the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) and the two test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (exact `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic, named only in `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs`): `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")` only, never in a release build. G2 exempts only a panic line at exactly `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs:<digits>` (founder ratification, Decisions Log `2026-09-28`). Another seam or environment read, a colour fact changing a control or reaching a log line, error or refusal, or another G2 exemption, needs a Decisions Log entry. Never add an env, flag or feature seam to force a refusing peer-euid decision: one account can make no foreign peer, so the decisions are proven over injected values (`peer_euid_admitted`, `serve_admitting`).

- NEVER let `config.json`, a `VIOLA_*` env var or a flag switch off a control. The two env carve-outs are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (exact `1`, forced fail-open hook panic; G2 exempts only its exact file path), both only under `fake-agent`, absent from release builds, switching off nothing; `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is read by the channel endpoint only to place the socket directory; the terminal colour facts `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM` are read in every build, only by `viola list`'s human mode and only to choose whether and how deep SGR bytes are written — they switch off no control, widen no redaction and are not a configuration channel (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline); another seam or environment read, or a colour fact changing a control or reaching a log line, error or refusal, needs its own Decisions Log entry. NEVER add an env, flag or feature seam to force a refusing peer-euid decision: one account can make no foreign peer, so the decisions are proven over injected values (`peer_euid_admitted`, `serve_admitting`).

- `.andromeda/security-plan.md` §Dependency Security, read whole by `rec.py render --section "Dependency Security"` — every action pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment, the permissions, the audits and what no workflow may do

- `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` §9 CI Integration, read whole by `rec.py render --section "CI Integration"` — the gates and their conditions (each fails closed; G2, G4 and the secret scan run even after a failed step; every upload only when the job's secret scan succeeded), kept true in `ci.yml`

- Time only through the injected `viola_core::Clock` (no mock_instant; `viola-mcp` runs no tokio timer, so no paused test clock — its `wait` bound is the pure `wait_timeout(given)`, a unit case), or an instant handed to a pure decision as an argument (the budget gate's `decide`); a link line's `since`, which `LinkSet::line` stamps from the wall clock outside the seam, is asserted by its shape only (`is_clock_time` in `tests/cli_links.rs`); never use an in-process clock to control another process's time.

- Every command but `logs` (which streams ndjson lines unless it fails) and `supervise` (which prints nothing) prints exactly one JSON document on stdout starting `{"v":1,"cmd":"<command>","ok":<bool>,…}`; exit 0 ok · 1 failure · 2 usage. A human-only message without the JSON document is forbidden.
- **5-command discipline:** boot / run / status / cleanup / logs — each but `logs` prints one JSON document `{"v":1,"cmd":…,"ok":…}` (`logs` streams ndjson lines unless it fails), exit 0/1/2

- **Non-path suites** — security sweep, error sanitization (no helper runs after each E2E test: the three surface witnesses, `tests/channel_error_bodies.rs`, `tests/cli_error_bodies.rs` and the MCP cases of `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`, and the enumeration and census of writers `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` replace it, reading the check in `tests/support/events.rs`; every `-32603` held at the unit layer), secret scan + canary (after each job's end-to-end run), schema conformance (G4 body), exit-cause matrix (`tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`, a root `cross_` binary: one negative test per cause of exit 21 and of exit 1 it holds, in both modes where a mode exists, a hint shared across causes failing the table; a cause its top comment names outside the table is a case of the binary its row names, the server-verification cause in `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs`, and the table holds the sixth closed cause `socket-dir-refused`, at exit 21 on a frame verb and at exit 1 on a start), security-control negatives (the Unix socket directory refusal in `tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs`, a Unix-only binary), `list` row integrity, cross-surface parity, chaos, property (7 parsers), contract

- Codes-only role files: `<home>/diagnostics/{run-<name>,hook-<name>,mcp,cli-<name>}.ndjson`; `mcp` always writes `mcp.ndjson` (D-09), no stderr fallback (a file that cannot be opened exits 1 printing nothing), never stdout (it carries MCP frames).
